subject: Implications of "Fail to factorize Q" message for models that do not ultimately fail

messages.author: 93a768cdebfde0f1
messages.subject: Implications of "Fail to factorize Q" message for models that do not ultimately fail
parts:
Hello all,
     I have a question related to the "fail to factorize Q" message (that has been a frequent topic of discussion on this group page) that occurs during model fitting. 

Example:

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 066a119c72db  date: Thu Jun 18 14:35:24 2015 +0200
	Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 829, Thread: 1
	Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...


My question(s) relates to the implications of this message. Is this failure only a problem if the "fix" doesn't work and the model ultimately fails afterwards? If model fitting does not fail, what implications does a series of "fail to factorize" instances occurring during model fitting hold for my results? Is it important to find a specification where the factorization of Q never fails, or should I expect this to occur at least a few times? About how many of these messages is "too many"? Or does this completely depend on the type/specification of model I am fitting?

Thanks in advance for your help. 

-tyler

Hi!

Good question.

A matrix can be numerically singular but not singular itself. Since, by
definition (if code and model is correct), the matrices factorized is
pos def, so this says that the precision matrix is numerical singular.
When this happens, then it adds a penalty preventing the step-size in
the optimization to be to large, which make the numerical singularity
goes away.

If this is happening once or twice only, then its ok. if it happens all
the time, like here

r = inla(y~1+x, data = data.frame(y=0,x=1),
control.fixed= list(prec = 0), verbose=T)

then the model is 'wrong' or badly specified.
